reviewed_finding: Mined the source declarations refineReport, refine_preserves, refine_separates (Paper.lean lines 59-66), supplied_tag_separates (Paper001.lean line 96, Fin 2 tag, one pair) and triangle_not_two_colored (Paper.lean line 69). The single-pair theorem is general and non-vacuous; the triangle theorem is a fixed three-Bool instance; the many-conflict statement (conflict graph, proper colouring, a 3-clique needs three colours) exists only as prose in paper.md section 9. This node proves the colouring characterisation, the odd-closed-walk obstruction and the fibre bit count in Lean for arbitrary relations/finite types, and tabulates all labelled graphs on up to 5 vertices natively. The sha256 of the three bound source files matches their operad pins (Paper.lean b0f6365d, Paper001.lean b9034069, DerivationDagQMClosure.lean c9ad9c23); the DerivationDagQMClosure theorem pg_to_sn_and_wdp_route_chain_composition is a conjunction of fixed arithmetic facts and does not mention refinement, so it supplies nothing here.

claim_boundary.supports: Kernel-checked and general over all types A, O, T: the refined report (q, t) keeps q as its first projection; a differing tag separates a pair (the source theorem refine_separates is this forward direction only); on a pair the old report collapses, the tag decides separation exactly (refine_separates_iff, new); refinement never merges what q separated. For a conflict relation C contained in the collapse of q: a GIVEN tag resolves every conflict iff it is proper for C (resolves_iff_proper); SOME b-bit tag (Fin b -> Bool) resolves every conflict iff C has a proper 2^b-colouring (refine_separates_many, an existence statement over tags). A Bool tag proper for C forbids any odd closed walk in C (so no triangle, no 5-cycle); this is the forward direction only, the converse (no odd closed walk implies a one-bit tag, Konig) is not in the kernel and is used natively (bipartite iff odd girth 0; one-bit tags 2^components when bipartite). For a finite type A in which every pair of distinct elements conflicts (a collapsed fibre taken as its own type, or q constant) a b-bit tag separating all pairs exists iff |A| <= 2^b (fibre_bits_iff; one bit iff |A| <= 2, fibre_one_bit_iff); for the fibre {a // q a = x} of an arbitrary report q some b-bit tag on the whole type resolves all conflicts between distinct fibre elements iff the fibre has at most 2^b elements (fibre_report_bits_iff). Native columns are counts over all (q, t) and ordered pairs (a, b), a = b allowed: quadruples = o^n t^n n^2; separated_by_tag = pairs with q a = q b and t a != t b; refined_equal = pairs with equal refined reports; old_separation_kept = pairs with q a != q b (all stay separated); iff_failures = pairs where equality of refined reports differs from equality of both components (0; the checker evaluates the refinement itself). Exact native tables: 14 named conflict graphs (components, proper one-bit tag counts 2^c or 0, chromatic number, minimal bits, odd girth), all labelled graphs on 1..5 vertices (labelled bipartite counts 1,2,7,41,376; minimal-bit distributions), fibre tag counts for m=1..5 and bits for m=6,8,9,17, and refinement counts for five small (n,o,t).
claim_boundary.does_not_support: Any algorithm, complexity or guarantee for FINDING a tag (the tables and the iff are existence statements, not search procedures); which tag a host should supply; the converse of the odd-closed-walk theorem in the kernel (Konig; native only); conflict graphs on more than 5 vertices beyond the 14 named ones; infinite carriers; any measurement, physical or interpretive reading of tags.
claim_boundary.narrowest_claim: For a report q and a conflict relation C inside its collapse, SOME b-bit tag resolves all conflicts iff C has a proper 2^b-colouring (refine_separates_many); a GIVEN tag resolves C iff it is proper (resolves_iff_proper). The source refine_separates is the forward direction for one pair; refine_separates_iff is the one-pair equivalence on collapsed pairs.
claim_boundary.next_test: First prove in Lean the converse of no_one_bit_of_odd_cycle (a finite symmetric conflict relation with no odd closed walk has a proper Bool tag), then that breadth-first 2-colouring is sound and complete for deciding it, as the first algorithmic statement about finding a tag; the present node proves existence criteria only.

second_review.notes: Cold read of the final run (profile, candidate, check_candidate.py, public cases, semantic_mutants.py, p2 lean.stdout.log, p4 host_check), lean4/RefineSeparates.lean (sha256 27eb9963 identical to p1/construction) and the DAG node, before the earlier pass. Statement fidelity: refine_retains, refine_separates (forward only), refine_separates_iff (hq : q a = q b), refine_keeps_old_separation, resolves_iff_proper (hC : every conflict is collapsed) and resolves_of_proper are what supports says. refine_separates_many is existential over tags and arbitrary C inside the collapse; bits_iff_colours transports Fin b -> Bool to Fin (2^b) via an equivalence from card equality, and the headline theorem is then essentially resolves_iff_proper plus that transport, i.e. correct but low-content. no_one_bit_of_odd_cycle really quantifies an odd closed walk f : Nat -> A with f n = f 0 and steps C (f i) (f (i+1)); the proof by parity induction is sound. fibre_bits_iff is for a finite type with the relation x <> y, and the new fibre_report_bits_iff is the actual fibre-of-a-report statement, with Resolves on the whole type and an explicit extension of the fibre tag by the constant false; I read the extension step in the proof and it is right. Axiom reports match the earlier description (none for the one-pair theorems, propext for the two iff theorems, classical triple for the card-based statements); the claim does not assert choice-freeness. Earlier-pass amendments: (a) all applied: the fibre sentence now cites fibre_bits_iff for a finite type with all pairs in conflict and the new fibre_report_bits_iff for a report fibre; narrowest_claim is the existential/per-tag pair of statements and says refine_separates is the forward direction; the refine columns (quadruples, separated_by_tag, refined_equal, old_separation_kept, iff_failures) are defined; the converse of the odd-closed-walk theorem (Konig) is declared native-only in supports and does_not_support; composition_tree uses a single C with the side condition C = C1 or C2 and proper_union_of_tags licenses it; next_test starts with the Lean converse; and refine_expected now evaluates the refinement on every (q, t, a, b) (so the iff is genuinely recomputed by the checker, not asserted), then requires the closed forms for separated_by_tag and old_separation_kept. The five missing near misses exist (refinement_iff_fails, tag_difference_separates_everything, petersen_is_four_chromatic, edgeless_needs_a_bit, dense_bipartite_is_not_bipartite). All 769 coordinate and 14 semantic mutants are rejected. (b) No weakening or hard-coded outcome: the checker uses union-find, BFS two-colouring, subset-DP chromatic number, bit_length(chi - 1), trace of A^k for odd girth, bitmask enumeration of all labelled graphs on 1..5 vertices with the identity sum over bipartite G of 2^c(G) = sum_k C(n,k) 2^(k(n-k)) (asserted), and falling factorials. I verified the labelled bipartite counts 1, 2, 7, 41, 376, the n = 3 pair identity (26), the 14 named-graph values (K5 chi 5 needs 3 bits, wheel5 chi 4, Petersen chi 3 and odd girth 5, K33 bipartite), and edgeless3 min_bits 0. (c) What I add: (i) the Konig direction is presupposed by 'bipartite iff odd girth 0' and 'one-bit tags = 2^components' in every graph record (the checker also asserts bipartite == (odd_girth == 0) as a consistency rule, which is not a Lean fact); the claim says so. (ii) The fibre_bits records for m = 6, 8, 9, 17 are the same formula (bit_length(m-1)) in producer and checker, with no enumeration of tags at those sizes; the evidence there is the Lean theorem, the native record adds nothing independent. (iii) The 'refine' records enumerate a tautology (equality of pairs); they test the producer and wire equality, not the mathematics, and the claim now says the checker evaluates the refinement itself. (iv) 'Satisfying many conflicts at once' in the DAG text is answered only at the level of existence = proper 2^b-colourability, which is the same finite combinatorial problem relabelled; no algorithmic statement and no hardness statement are made, and none is claimed. (v) next_test (Lean converse of the odd-cycle theorem, then BFS soundness and completeness) is the node's own obligation, but its first step is literally the second clause of does_not_support (the Konig converse) and its second step is the first clause (finding algorithms); it is the discharge of those clauses rather than an independent test, acceptable but at the edge of the 'not equal to does_not_support' requirement.

For a conflict relation inside the collapse of q, some b-bit tag resolves every conflict iff the relation has a proper 2^b-colouring (refine_separates_many); an odd closed walk forbids one bit (forward direction only; the converse, Konig, is native-only), and a finite type with all pairs in conflict needs ceil(log2 m) bits. dag_suggestion.statement: A supplied tag t separates a collapsed pair exactly when it differs there, and the refined report (q, t) keeps q as its first projection and never merges what q separated. For a conflict relation inside the collapse of q, some b-bit tag resolves every conflict iff the relation has a proper 2^b-colouring (an odd closed walk forbids one bit; a finite type with all pairs in conflict needs ceil(log2 m) bits). Finding such a tag, its cost, and the one-bit converse (Konig) in the kernel are not addressed.

earlier_pass.notes: Cold read of specsB/PG-REFINE-SEPARATES.json, refine_separates_{check,format,semantic,spec}.py, lean4/RefineSeparates.lean (compiled, exit 0; no axioms for the one-pair theorems, propext only for the two iff theorems, propext+Quot.sound for the odd-cycle theorems, the full classical triple for the card-based bit statements), pfp_refine_separates.py, the operad yaml and the DAG node. The Lean statements are what they are cited for in four of the five places that matter: refine_retains, refine_separates, refine_separates_iff (collapsed pair), resolves_iff_proper (hC makes properness equivalent to resolution for an arbitrary relation C), bits_iff_colours, no_one_bit_of_odd_cycle (genuine odd closed walk f : Nat -> A with f n = f 0), and refine_separates_many (arbitrary types, arbitrary C inside the collapse). The numeric tables are right: labelled bipartite counts 1,2,7,41,376, by_min_bits sum to 2^C(n,2), the falling factorials (2^b)_m, the 14 named graphs (K5 needs 3 bits, wheel5 chi 4, Petersen chi 3 odd girth 5), and the refine counts (e.g. (2,2,2): 64, 8, 40, 16). The checker is independent of the producer in algorithm (union-find, BFS, subset DP, trace of A^k versus DFS, exhaustive tags, backtracking, BFS levels) and checks the identity sum 2^c(G) = sum_k C(n,k) 2^(k(n-k)). Problems: (1) The fibre statement in supports ('a collapsed fibre of size m admits a b-bit separating tag iff m <= 2^b') is not what fibre_bits_iff states: that theorem is about a finite type A with the complete conflict relation x != y, with no report q and no fibre; the collapsed-fibre reading needs A := the fibre as a subtype or q constant, and the extension of a fibre tag to the ambient type is not formalised. (2) narrowest_claim 'a b-bit supplied tag resolves all conflicts iff C has a proper 2^b-colouring' reads as a statement about a given tag; the theorem is existential over tags (refine_separates_many) and the per-tag statement is resolves_iff_proper; and 'refine_separates is the one-conflict case' is only the forward direction (the one-pair iff is refine_separates_iff). (3) For the refine records the checker asserts iff_failures = 0 as a constant and the other columns are closed forms that already embed the theorem (refined_equal = n o^n t^n + n(n-1) o^(n-1) t^(n-1), old_separation_kept = n(n-1) o^(n-1)(o-1) t^n); only the producer enumerates, so the iff is tested natively by the producer alone. (4) The profile never defines quadruples, separated_by_tag, refined_equal, old_separation_kept: they are counts over (q, t, a, b) with ordered pairs including a = b; separated_by_tag counts only collapsed pairs with differing tags, old_separation_kept counts every pair with q a != q b. (5) The converse of the odd-cycle theorem (no odd closed walk implies a 2-colouring) is not in Lean; it is used natively as the checker rule bipartite == (odd_girth == 0) and by the one_bit_tags = 2^components formula; supports states only the forward direction, which is right, but the tables presuppose Konig's theorem, which the next_test (BFS soundness/completeness) would settle. (6) composition_tree has the input 'C1 or C2' for proper_tag_test: there is no generator forming a union of conflict relations, and the checked composition's licensing relation is many_conflicts_iff_proper_colouring although the theorem that licenses it is proper_union (no relation of that name). Mutants are consistent misreadings and each is caught; missing near misses are listed. next_test is the node's own unpaid obligation (a first algorithmic statement), distinct from does_not_support though it is the first step of its first item.
amendments: supports, fibre clause: replace 'a collapsed fibre of size m admits a b-bit separating tag iff m <= 2^b (so ceil(log2 m) bits)' by 'for a finite type A in which every pair of distinct elements conflicts (for instance a collapsed fibre taken as its own type, or q constant), a b-bit tag separating all pairs exists iff |A| <= 2^b (fibre_bits_iff; one bit iff |A| <= 2, fibre_one_bit_iff)'. Or add a Lean theorem for a fibre F = {a // q a = x} of an arbitrary q : A -> O: (exists t : A -> (Fin b -> Bool), Resolves q t (fun a a' => q a = x and q a' = x and a != a')) iff card F <= 2^b.

narrowest_claim: replace with 'For a report q and a conflict relation C inside its collapse, some b-bit tag resolves all conflicts iff C has a proper 2^b-colouring (refine_separates_many); a given tag resolves C iff it is proper (resolves_iff_proper). The source refine_separates is the forward direction for one pair; refine_separates_iff is the one-pair equivalence on collapsed pairs.'

supports, native clause: define the refine columns: 'quadruples = o^n t^n n^2 triples (q, t) with ordered pairs (a, b), a = b allowed; separated_by_tag = pairs with q a = q b and t a != t b; refined_equal = pairs with equal refined reports; old_separation_kept = pairs with q a != q b (all of which stay separated); iff_failures = number of pairs where equality of refined reports differs from equality of both components'.

supports/relation odd_closed_walk_refuses_one_bit: add 'the converse (no odd closed walk implies a proper 2-colouring) is not in the kernel; it is used natively (bipartite iff odd girth 0, one-bit tags = 2^components when bipartite) and is König's theorem'.

profile.composition_tree item 2: replace 'proper_tag_test(C1 or C2, tag_pair(t1, t2))' by 'proper_tag_test(C, tag_pair(t1, t2))' with the side condition C = C1 or C2, and add the relation 'proper_union' (proper t1 for C1 and proper t2 for C2 give proper (t1, t2) for C1 or C2; kernel proper_union) as the licensing relation of the checked composition.

next_test: keep, but prefix 'First prove the converse of no_one_bit_of_odd_cycle in Lean (no odd closed walk implies a proper Bool tag, for a finite symmetric C), then ...'; the BFS statement is a corollary-level algorithmic claim, the converse is the immediately missing existence statement.
defects: supports 'a collapsed fibre of size m admits a b-bit separating tag iff m <= 2^b': fibre_bits_iff is stated for a type A with relation x != y, not for a fibre of a report, and the extension step is not formalised. Corrected wording above.

narrowest_claim 'a b-bit supplied tag resolves all conflicts iff C has a proper 2^b-colouring' is existential over tags; as written it can be read as a statement for a given tag. Corrected wording above.

narrowest_claim 'the source single-pair theorem refine_separates is the one-conflict case': refine_separates is the forward implication only; the iff is new (refine_separates_iff). Corrected wording above.

Checker refine rule: iff_failures is a constant 0 in refine_expected and the three other columns are closed forms that assume the theorem; the checker never evaluates a refinement, so the iff is tested only by the producer's enumeration. A wrong certificate cannot pass (it would differ from the constants), but the independence claim in independent_predicates ('refinement counts by closed forms') should say that this record is an arithmetic check of the theorem, not a recomputation.
supports uses the unexplained column names quadruples, separated_by_tag, refined_equal, old_separation_kept; definitions above.

The odd-cycle converse (König) is used natively but is not a Lean anchor; supports states only the forward direction, so no false sentence, but the relation text 'native tables: every native graph with positive odd girth has zero one-bit tags' conceals that the equivalence bipartite == odd girth 0 is a native assumption.

composition_tree 'proper_tag_test(C1 or C2, ...)' uses a conflict-union constructor that is not a generator; checked_composition's licensing_relations name many_conflicts_iff_proper_colouring where proper_union is the licensing theorem.

Missing near-miss mutants: (a) refinement merges old reports: iff_failures = 1 at (3,2,2) (the existing refinement_merges_old only sets old_separation_kept = 0, which the closed form also rejects, but it does not exhibit the iff failing); (b) tag difference separates every pair regardless of q (converse of refine_separates on non-collapsed pairs): set separated_by_tag at (3,2,2) to 192, the number of (q, t, a, b) with t a != t b whether or not q a = q b, instead of 96; (c) petersen read as triangle-containing or 4-chromatic (odd_girth 3, chi 4) to separate odd girth from chromatic number; (d) edgeless3 with min_bits 1 (zero bits suffice when there is no conflict); (e) k33 read as non-bipartite because it is dense (one_bit_tags 0).
